page.h1: HTS Chapter 30: Pharmaceutical Products — Foreign Tariff Changes on U.S. Exports

seo.title: Tariffs on U.S. Pharmaceutical Exports: What Changed Since 2025 (HTS Ch. 30) | KoalaGains
seo.shortDescription: Every tariff action since January 2025 that touched U.S. medicine exports: China’s retaliation (125% → 10%), Canada and EU counter-tariff lists, trade deals with the UK, Japan, Switzerland and the EU, and Brazil’s WTO challenge.

intro:
What **other countries** changed on U.S. pharmaceuticals since January 2025, and what is coming. The only new measure that costs U.S. medicine exporters money is **China's extra 10%** on all U.S. goods — and it could rise to 34% if the suspension of the rest lapses on **January 10, 2027**. China's older 2019 counter-tariffs still reach some dressings and 3006 goods unless the buyer holds an exclusion, and the exclusions end on **December 31, 2026**.

Canada's counter-tariff lists left Chapter 30 out; the EU's list named only adhesive dressings and has never been applied. The 2025–26 deals with the UK, Japan, Switzerland and the EU did not need to cut tariffs that were already zero. For what the U.S. charges on imported medicines, see the import Tariff updates page.
scope: The 8 largest markets for U.S. Chapter 30 goods (85% of 2025 exports; the EU counts as one market). Actions on other U.S. goods are listed only where a buyer might reasonably expect them to reach medicines.

upcoming.title: China's tariff exclusions for U.S. goods end
upcoming.whatHappens: China's exclusions from its 2019 counter-tariffs on U.S. goods are valid until December 31, 2026 under the November 2025 U.S.–China deal.
upcoming.impact: Any exclusion a buyer holds would end, so listed Chapter 30 goods — mainly dressings (3005) and 3006 goods such as reagents and dental cements — would pay China's 2019 counter-tariffs again. Vaccines, antibodies and most packaged medicines are not on those lists.

upcoming.title: China's suspension of 24 points of its extra tariff on U.S. goods ends
upcoming.whatHappens: China suspended 24 points of its extra tariff on all U.S. goods for one year from November 10, 2025, keeping 10%. In September 2026 the two sides agreed to extend the arrangement to January 10, 2027, with talks on a further extension expected before the end of the year.
upcoming.impact: If it lapses, China's extra tariff on U.S. Chapter 30 goods goes from 10% to 34% on top of its 0–3% normal rate: a $1M shipment of U.S. antibodies would pay about $370,000 instead of $130,000.
upcoming.status: Extension to Jan 10, 2027 announced by MOFCOM; China's Tariff Commission has not yet published its notice

inEffect.measure: Extra tariff on all U.S. goods (State Council Tariff Commission)
inEffect.appliesTo: All Chapter 30 goods of U.S. origin, on top of China's 0–3% normal rate (5–10% on dressings and other 3006 goods).
inEffect.whatItMeans: A $1M shipment of U.S. antibodies pays about $130,000 instead of $30,000 at China's 3% normal rate. The extra rate peaked at 125% in April 2025; a further 24 points are suspended, now until January 10, 2027 — see What's coming.

changes.title: U.S.–China Board of Trade product lists
changes.status: Recommended for reduced tariffs; no Chinese tariff cut published yet
changes.detail: China’s import list under the U.S.–China Board of Trade “30-for-30” framework names 1,619 Chinese tariff lines that could get lower tariffs on U.S. goods. Only three are in Chapter 30: other adhesive dressings (3005.10.90), other wadding and gauze (3005.90.90) and dental and bone cements (3006.40.00). No vaccines, antibodies or packaged medicines.

changes.title: Counter-tariffs on U.S. products (answering U.S. Section 338 tariffs)
changes.detail: Mostly steel, aluminum, dairy, appliances, furniture and clothing. The list jumps from Chapter 19 to perfumes (3303), skipping pharmaceuticals entirely.

changes.title: Brazil has imposed nothing on U.S. goods; it is challenging U.S. tariffs at the WTO
changes.status: Nothing imposed on U.S. goods; talks ongoing
changes.detail: Brazil has published no countermeasure on U.S. goods. Its Economic Reciprocity Law (Law 15,122 of April 11, 2025) would allow them — such as import restrictions or suspending intellectual-property obligations — but none has been applied. On July 27, 2026 Brazil asked the United States for WTO consultations over U.S. tariffs on Brazilian goods, and Brazilian ministers met USTR on August 31 and September 30, 2026 to set up a working group on a possible agreement.

changes.title: USMCA stays in force: Canada and Mexico keep 0% on qualifying U.S. goods
changes.detail: At the first USMCA joint review on July 1, 2026 the three countries did not agree to a new 16-year term, so the agreement is now reviewed every year; it stays in force until at least July 1, 2036. Canada and Mexico keep applying USMCA rates to qualifying U.S. goods.

changes.title: EU–U.S. framework tariff cuts adopted
changes.detail: Regulation (EU) 2026/1455 cuts EU duties on listed U.S. goods to zero from July 1, 2026, and Regulation (EU) 2026/1461 sets aside duties on certain other goods. No Chapter 30 line is listed because EU duties on U.S. medicines were already zero.

changes.title: Mexico raises its general tariffs on goods from countries without a trade agreement
changes.status: In force since Jan 1, 2026; U.S. goods still enter under USMCA
changes.detail: The decree raises Mexico's general (MFN) rates on more than 1,400 tariff lines, mostly cars, textiles, clothing, steel, plastics and footwear. No Chapter 30 line is listed, and U.S. goods that qualify for USMCA keep their preferential rate. Mexico has published no counter-tariff on U.S. goods.

changes.title: Reciprocity petition against the 2025 U.S. tariffs: framing approved, action deferred
changes.detail: Camex's executive committee (Gecex) approved the Foreign Ministry's petition as falling under the Economic Reciprocity Law and chose to await diplomatic consultations before forming the working group that would propose countermeasures. Nothing was imposed.

changes.title: U.S.–UK pharmaceutical pricing arrangement
changes.status: In force; full text agreed Apr 2, 2026
changes.detail: Not a tariff: the UK raises the net price it pays for new medicines by about 25% and lifts NICE’s cost-effectiveness threshold, which should help U.S. drug sales. UK tariffs on medicines stay at zero.

changes.title: U.S.–Switzerland–Liechtenstein trade framework
changes.detail: Switzerland intends to apply zero duties on all U.S. industrial goods, including medicines.

changes.title: China extends its tariff exclusions for U.S. goods to December 31, 2026
changes.detail: Under the November 2025 U.S.–China deal, China extended its market-based exclusion process for imports from the United States; exclusions stay valid until December 31, 2026. They lift China's 2019 counter-tariffs on U.S. goods (answering the U.S. Section 301 tariffs), which were never repealed. For Chapter 30 those lists still name mainly dressings (3005) and 3006 goods such as reagents, dental cements and first-aid kits — for example 10% on 3006.40, 3006.50 and 3006.70 — but not vaccines, antibodies or most packaged medicines.

changes.title: U.S.–Japan agreement
changes.detail: Executive Order 14345 implements the U.S.–Japan agreement: Japan works toward buying U.S. farm and other goods worth $8 billion a year and investing in the U.S.; Japanese tariffs on medicines did not change.

changes.title: EU countermeasures on about €93B of U.S. goods
changes.detail: Implementing Regulation (EU) 2025/1564 listed one Chapter 30 code, adhesive dressings (CN 3005 10 00), at an extra 10% from September 7, 2025; medicines in 3001–3004 were not listed. The measures were suspended from August 6, 2025, again from February 7, 2026, and from August 7, 2026 with no end date (Implementing Regulation (EU) 2026/1893).

changes.title: Extra tariff on all U.S. goods cut to 10%
changes.status: In force; 24-point suspension extended to Jan 10, 2027
changes.detail: Rose 34% → 84% → 125% in April 2025 (125% from April 12), then cut to 10% from May 14, 2025 with 24 points suspended for 90 days. The suspension was extended for 90 days from August 12, 2025 and for one year from November 10, 2025, with the 10% kept. In September 2026 the two sides agreed to extend the arrangement to January 10, 2027. Applies to medicines on top of China’s normal rate.

changes.title: U.S.–UK Economic Prosperity Deal
changes.detail: UK concessions were a beef quota and a duty-free ethanol quota; UK tariffs on medicines were already zero.

changes.title: 25% counter-tariff on C$30B of U.S. goods
changes.detail: The list jumped from silica sand (2505) to perfumes (3303); no pharmaceuticals. Canada repealed most of it on Sept 1, 2025, keeping only steel, aluminum and auto surtaxes.
